preconditions.description: The length of the string s is between 3 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all('A' <= c <= 'Z' for c in s)
preconditions.description: All characters in the string s are uppercase English letters.
The string s contains at least three different characters.

postconditions.expression: all(ord(return_value[i]) >= ord(return_value[i+1]) for i in range(len(return_value)-1))
postconditions.description: The characters in the returned string are in descending order of their ASCII values.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == max(len(subseq) for subseq in subsequences if is_arithmetic(subseq))
postconditions.description: The returned string is the longest subsequence of s that is in arithmetic progression.

postconditions.expression: all(ord(return_value[i]) - ord(return_value[i+1]) == ord(return_value[0]) - ord(return_value[1]) for i in range(len(return_value)-1))
postconditions.description: The characters in the returned string have a common difference in their ASCII values.

postconditions.expression: all(ord(return_value[i]) >= ord(return_value[j]) for i in range(len(return_value)) for j in range(len(return_value)) if ord(return_value[i]) - ord(return_value[j]) == ord(return_value[0]) - ord(return_value[1]))
postconditions.description: Among all longest arithmetic progressions, the returned string has the highest ASCII values.
